Use a durable queue with bounded concurrency, per-tenant/user quotas, exponential backoff with a retry budget, dead-letter handling, cancellation, and a polling/SSE status endpoint. Deduplicate identical jobs, cache only policy-compatible assets, sign short-lived asset URLs, and record correlation IDs from request through moderation, generation, storage, and delivery.

6. **[SRE/Cost] Enforce hard caps before dispatch.** Maintain a server-side allowance ledger for daily/monthly image credits, maximum panels per turn, pixel/quality tiers, concurrency, storage, and retry spend. Reserve estimated cost before dispatch, settle against actual usage, release unused reservation, and atomically reject or downgrade when the cap is reached. Adult Free should have a transparent daily allowance and text fallback; Kid Mode should be ad-free with an explicit non-advertising quota; Play later should queue or save text/scene plans without silently charging for images. Add global circuit breakers, provider/model spend ceilings, anomaly alerts, and a kill switch. Never use deceptive countdowns, forced upsells, or dark-pattern consent.

7. **[QA/Release] Build a risk-based evaluation set.** Maintain golden cases for character continuity, panel readability, captions/OCR, multilingual text, accessibility, policy boundaries, adversarial prompts, cache isolation, duplicate delivery, retries, and ledger invariants. Test at least one safe and unsafe case per policy category and language supported at launch; compare policy/model/style versions using blinded human review plus automated checks. Canary new model/style/prompt versions behind feature flags and roll back without rewriting historical events.

8. **[Analytics/Support] Measure safety and experience without over-collecting.** Emit privacy-minimised events for turn committed, job queued/started/completed/failed, moderation block/appeal, fallback, cap hit, latency, and asset abandonment. Keep Kid Mode analytics aggregated or pseudonymous, exclude ad identifiers, and define retention/deletion schedules. Support should receive a user-visible incident ID, reproducible turn metadata, moderation reason category, and safe replay path; operators must be able to quarantine an asset/style version and notify affected users without exposing sensitive prompts or child data.

9. **[Integrity/Media] Label AI-generated panels and preserve provenance.** Attach an internal manifest with model, prompt-template/style versions, moderation result, and source/reference declarations; where media leaves the product, consider a standards-based provenance manifest such as C2PA and a visible AI-generated label. Strip unnecessary EXIF and personal metadata, enforce upload rights/consent, and prevent public indexing of private assets. **Copyright, likeness, disclosure, and platform/store requirements require counsel and official verification.**

10. **[Localization/Accessibility] Localise policy as well as strings.** Translate UI, safety explanations, refusal text, captions, and support flows with human review; maintain locale-specific blocked-term and context tests rather than literal word lists. Provide alt text or a concise scene description, keyboard navigation, reduced-motion options, readable caption contrast, and a text-only mode. Do not infer a child’s age, vulnerability, or identity from language or image characteristics without a documented lawful and fairness review.
output.risks: Primary failures include unsafe or sexualised imagery slipping through because text-only filters miss visual/OCR context; minor-age ambiguity and weak age assurance exposing children to adult content; character/style drift, hallucinated text, and culturally poor translations reducing trust; retries, duplicate jobs, cache leakage, or client-side quota enforcement causing ledger corruption or runaway spend; adversarial prompts, uploads, real-person likenesses, copyright claims, and prompt injection bypassing controls; and excessive telemetry or parental features creating UK GDPR, transparency, retention, or profiling exposure. Availability failures can strand a committed turn unless text fallback and durable job state exist. Legal, Online Safety Act, age-assurance, advertising, copyright, and store-policy conclusions must be verified with UK counsel and the relevant official bodies before launch.

results.input: Localization, regional authenticity, locale-aware language generation, English locale QA, accessibility, and UI-string operations

output.exit_criteria:
1. 100% of player-visible strings are externalized, keyed, documented, versioned, and covered by missing-key, placeholder, markup, overflow, and snapshot CI checks; zero unresolved P0/P1 string defects.
2. `en-GB` passes the full route/state matrix across supported browsers, mobile widths, 200–400% zoom, keyboard-only navigation, and screen-reader smoke tests, with zero release-blocking WCAG 2.2 AA findings and all residual issues risk-accepted by the Accessibility Lead.
3. At least 95% of sampled generated turns meet schema, locale, glossary, mode, and safety assertions automatically; 100% of high-impact consent, privacy, safety, monetization, and mode-switch strings pass human UK-native editorial review.
4. Regional review completes with documented participants and decisions; zero open critical stereotype, invented-fact, materially misleading UK convention, or harmful representation issues, and every exception has an owner and rollback plan.
5. Locale fallback rate for intended `en-GB` sessions is below 0.5% in staging and can be traced to an approved missing-resource case; no fallback changes canonical ledger values or replay output semantics.
6. Kid Mode has a documented DPIA/child-impact assessment where applicable, high-privacy defaults, ad-free verification, no targeted profiling or dark-pattern nudges, clear mode indication, and counsel/official verification of age, privacy, advertising, consumer, and platform/store obligations before release.
7. Accessibility controls—including text resize, reduced motion, captions/transcripts where relevant, pause/replay, simplification without data loss, and error/turn announcements—are tested with representative users or qualified evaluators, with findings closed or explicitly risk-accepted.
8. Telemetry is minimised, retention-limited, access-controlled, and tested not to collect raw child narrative by default; locale and accessibility dashboards show baseline metrics, alert thresholds, and an on-call owner.
9. Kill switches, locale-bundle rollback, model-policy rollback, support escalation, and incident drills complete successfully in staging, with recovery objectives agreed by Release Management and Trust & Safety.
10. Launch approvals and evidence are signed by Localization, Regional Editorial, Accessibility, QA, Trust & Safety, Privacy/Security, Product, and Legal; all legal/store items remain marked **pending counsel or official verification** until confirmed.
output.mechanisms:
1. **Locale contract and fallback (Owner: Platform/Localization).** Store a BCP 47 locale per profile/session, separate language from region, and keep ledger/event serialization locale-neutral (UTC timestamps, stable IDs, canonical numerics). Use deterministic fallback `en-GB → en → product default`; never infer locale from IP alone. Format dates, numbers, plural forms, relative time, and list punctuation with ECMAScript `Intl`/CLDR-compatible APIs, while preserving the raw ledger value for replay and audit. [1] [2]
2. **English-first UK baseline (Owner: UX Writing/Editorial).** Define `en-GB` as an explicit locale, with a glossary covering spelling, punctuation, dates, units, currency, fantasy terminology, safety labels, age-mode labels, and UI verbs. Use plain, direct sentences, avoid idioms that impair comprehension, and distinguish “Free,” “Kid Mode,” and “Play later” without pressure or ambiguity. Treat “adult” as an access/content classification, not as a euphemism for sexual content; have counsel verify age, advertising, privacy, and store/platform claims before launch.
3. **Locale-aware AI generation (Owner: Applied AI/Editorial).** Pass the selected locale, region, register, content rating, mode, glossary, and canonical game-state schema as structured generation inputs. Require the model to emit stable machine-readable fields separately from player-facing prose. Add terminology constraints, forbidden untranslated tokens, unit/date rules, and a “do not invent regional facts” instruction; when a cultural reference is uncertain, prefer a neutral alternative or ask the player. Preserve original and rendered text plus model/version/prompt policy metadata for replay and incident review.
4. **Regional authenticity review (Owner: Regional Editor/Research).** Maintain a UK reference pack for names, geography, institutions, folklore, dialect boundaries, currency/measure conventions, and sensitive historical/cultural references. Label fictional material as fictional, do not present generated claims as authoritative local knowledge, and run review panels with UK-native players from varied regions and backgrounds. Track an issue taxonomy—wrong register, imported US usage, stereotype, anachronism, invented place/fact, and harmful representation—with severity and rollback ownership.
5. **String externalization and UI operations (Owner: Client Engineering/Localization Operations).** Prohibit hard-coded player-visible strings. Give every string a stable key, description/context, character-length guidance, placeholders with types, rich-text restrictions, screenshot or component reference, source locale, owner, and review state. Use ICU MessageFormat-style plural/select branches where supported; never concatenate translated fragments. Validate missing keys, duplicate keys, malformed placeholders, unescaped markup, truncation, overflow, RTL contamination, and unexpected line breaks in CI. Version locale bundles with the game build and support additive, reversible hotfixes.
6. **AI-generated text QA harness (Owner: QA/Applied AI).** Build golden scenarios for combat, exploration, failure, consent/safety boundaries, tutorial, account recovery, Kid Mode, ad-free claims, and offline/Play-later recovery. For each locale, test deterministic seeds where possible and property-based assertions for schema validity, prohibited content, required labels, terminology, units, and state consistency. Add human linguistic review for high-impact strings and sample generated narrative; log defect rate by locale and severity rather than relying only on aggregate quality scores.
7. **Accessibility as a release gate (Owner: Accessibility Lead/Frontend).** Target WCAG 2.2 AA as the product benchmark, even though public-sector-specific UK regulations may not directly apply to a private game; counsel must verify applicable Equality Act, consumer, platform, and jurisdictional obligations. Ensure keyboard-complete play, visible focus, semantic headings/landmarks, screen-reader announcements for turns and errors, accessible form labels, text resizing/reflow, contrast, non-colour cues, reduced motion, no flashing hazards, captions/transcripts for audio, and a non-timed path for reading AI output. [3] [4]
8. **Accessible language and cognition controls (Owner: UX/Accessibility/Content).** Offer adjustable text size/line height, readable width, pause/replay, “shorter explanation” and “simplify” controls, explicit status summaries, predictable navigation, and user-controlled animation/audio. Do not make simplification destructive: retain the canonical narrative and ledger, show what was condensed, and let the player restore full text. Test with screen readers, keyboard-only users, low vision, dyslexia/cognitive access needs, mobile browsers, zoom, and poor connectivity.
9. **Kid Mode protections and neutral choice architecture (Owner: Trust & Safety/Product/Legal).** Make Kid Mode defaults privacy-preserving and ad-free as specified; disable targeted advertising, profiling, unnecessary data collection, geolocation, and social/contact discovery unless counsel and the relevant official guidance confirm a lawful, necessary design. Do not use nudges to weaken privacy, prolong play, or convert a child into an adult mode. Keep adult Free and Kid Mode visibly distinct, provide a clear mode indicator, and prevent accidental mode switching with a proportionate, accessible confirmation flow. The ICO Children’s Code contains 15 standards covering best interests, DPIAs, age-appropriate application, transparency, defaults, minimisation, parental controls, profiling, and nudges; treat applicability and age-assurance choices as legal work requiring official verification. [5]
10. **English locale QA matrix (Owner: Release QA).** Test `en-GB` on desktop and mobile widths, zoom 200–400%, long names, apostrophes/curly quotes, £ amounts, 12/24-hour preferences, daylight-saving transitions, plural edge cases, missing/late model output, empty states, errors, cookies/consent, and all mode labels. Include snapshot tests for every route and state, plus exploratory native-UK review; block release on clipped, ambiguous, misleading, or inaccessible copy.
11. **Translation and future-locale readiness (Owner: Localization Operations/Engineering).** Design for expansion and contraction, gender/plural variation, grammatical ordering, non-Latin scripts, RTL, and locale-specific fonts before adding languages. Keep source copy translator-friendly, avoid embedded punctuation and culturally bound metaphors, and require back-translation or in-context review for safety, monetization, consent, and mode-switch strings. Do not launch a locale merely because machine translation passes automated checks.
12. **Telemetry and support loop (Owner: Analytics/Support).** Instrument locale, mode, client version, string key, fallback use, generation validation failures, player language correction, accessibility setting usage, and support category with data minimisation and retention limits. Never log raw child narrative or sensitive free text by default. Publish an internal locale-quality dashboard with severity-weighted defects, fallback rate, accessibility failures, and rollback status; provide an accessible “wrong language/wording/accessibility” report path and route urgent safety or child-privacy issues to Trust & Safety and Legal.
13. **Launch governance (Owner: Release Manager).** Require signed approvals from Localization, UK Regional Editorial, Accessibility, QA, Trust & Safety, Security/Privacy, Product, and Legal for the launch matrix. Maintain a kill switch for locale bundles and model-generated content modes, a rapid rollback to the last known-good bundle/policy, an incident playbook, and a public accessibility/contact route. Store evidence: test reports, reviewed string inventory, DPIA where applicable, accessibility findings, regional review decisions, and counsel/official verification of legal/store items.
output.risks: Primary failure modes are US-centric or stereotyped UK representation; hallucinated local facts, dialect, or institutions; inconsistent locale handling that corrupts ledger replay; untranslated, truncated, or placeholder-broken UI; AI prose that violates mode, age, safety, or terminology constraints; inaccessible turn updates, focus, motion, contrast, or dense narrative; accidental adult/Kid Mode crossover; privacy-invasive telemetry or child profiling; machine-translation errors in consent, safety, advertising, or mode-switch copy; and legal or platform claims treated as settled without counsel or official verification. Automated checks cannot establish cultural authenticity, accessibility, or legal compliance on their own.

results.input: Schema evolution, save migrations, disaster recovery, support operations, trust-and-safety escalation, and incident communications

output.exit_criteria:
1. 100% of persisted saves and ledger events have validated version metadata; migration code has automated tests for every supported version, including malformed and adversarial fixtures.
2. A production-shaped dry run completes with 0 invariant violations, 0 unexplained row-count/checksum differences, bounded lock time, and a documented pause/resume and recovery result.
3. At least 99.9% of sampled legacy saves load or are safely quarantined with a player/support recovery path; no save is silently discarded; replayed turn outcomes meet the agreed deterministic-equivalence or documented compatibility tolerance.
4. Restore drills meet approved RPO/RTO targets for ledger, snapshots, projections, configuration, and entitlements; two consecutive drills pass checksum, referential-integrity, save-load, and turn-replay checks.
5. Backup freshness, restore success, migration errors, ledger/projection divergence, save-load failures, moderation actions, and escalation latency have alert thresholds, named on-call owners, and tested pages.
6. 100% of support-console privileged actions are reason-coded, least-privilege controlled, time-limited where elevated, and present in immutable audit logs; access review and transcript-redaction tests pass.
7. Trust & Safety has completed documented red-team suites for adult and Kid Mode, including prompt injection, evasion, grooming, sexual content, self-harm, violence, doxxing, and mode-confusion cases; all critical findings are closed or formally risk-accepted by the accountable executive and safeguarding lead.
8. Severity-1 tabletop and live-failover exercises demonstrate named incident command, evidence preservation, internal escalation, player messaging, status-page updates, and a post-incident review; first player-facing update meets the committed SLA.
9. DPO/legal/safeguarding sign-off records the DPIA, Children’s Code assessment, Online Safety Act/Ofcom applicability, age assurance, retention/deletion, reporting, advertising, and any store or platform requirements; unresolved items are explicitly marked pending counsel/official verification.
10. Support launch rehearsal resolves representative gameplay, account, privacy, restore, safeguarding, and abuse reports within severity SLAs, with successful warm handoff and appeal/correction handling.
output.mechanisms:
1. **Schema evolution — [Engineering owner]**: Use additive, backward-compatible changes first: nullable/new fields, new enum values handled as “unknown,” dual-read/dual-write only for bounded migrations, and explicit `schema_version` plus `content_version` on every ledger event and save snapshot. Keep immutable append-only ledger events; derive mutable projections so a failed projection rebuild cannot rewrite player history. Require migration manifests with preconditions, transformed-row counts, checksums, idempotency, and a tested down/forward recovery path. Gate destructive changes behind a deprecation window and feature flags; contract-test old and new clients against representative saves.

2. **Save migration — [Game/backend owner]**: Treat each save format as a versioned document with pure, deterministic migration functions (`vN -> vN+1`), never an in-place opaque script. Migrate on read into a temporary representation, validate invariants, then persist a new snapshot while retaining the original. Use canary cohorts, dry runs on production-shaped copies, sampled replay of turns, and automatic quarantine of saves that fail validation. Expose a player-visible recovery path: restore prior checkpoint, export/download where appropriate, and support-assisted repair; do not silently discard progress.

3. **Release and rollback — [Release/SRE owner]**: Separate expand, migrate, contract phases; deploy code that understands both versions before backfilling, then remove old paths only after an evidence-based retention period. Use transactional batches, rate limits, pause/resume checkpoints, lock-time budgets, and a kill switch. Roll back application code independently from data transforms; for irreversible transforms, restore from snapshot or replay the immutable ledger rather than pretending a code rollback restores data.

4. **Backups and disaster recovery — [SRE + security owner]**: Maintain encrypted, access-controlled, geographically separated backups of ledger, snapshots, metadata, configuration, and key recovery material. Apply least privilege, separate backup credentials, tamper-evident/auditable retention, and malware/ransomware isolation. Define service-specific RPO/RTO, including an explicit maximum acceptable loss of turns and entitlement changes. Run scheduled restore tests into an isolated environment, verify checksums and referential integrity, and perform game-level checks (load save, replay turns, regenerate projection) rather than only database-level success. NCSC guidance explicitly recommends practising restoration and copying only clean data back to clean systems [2].

5. **Support operations — [Support lead]**: Build an authenticated support console with least-privilege roles, reason-coded access, immutable audit logs, redacted transcript views, and time-limited elevation. Support actions should be reversible, idempotent, and ledgered: restore checkpoint, re-run projection, grant a documented make-good, or place an account/save in quarantine. Publish status, known-issue, refund/entitlement, deletion/export, and safeguarding routes. Define SLAs by severity, a warm handoff to Trust & Safety, and a clear distinction between gameplay bugs, account compromise, privacy requests, and child-safety reports. Do not ask players to reveal unnecessary personal data or use manipulative retention language.

6. **Trust-and-safety escalation — [Trust & Safety lead + safeguarding duty officer]**: Maintain separate adult Free and Kid Mode policy bundles, with Kid Mode defaulting to the strictest age-appropriate content, privacy, logging, and interaction settings. Use layered detection: input/output classifiers, deterministic blocklists/rules, rate limits, abuse reports, and human review for high-severity or ambiguous cases. Log policy version, model version, classifier result, action, and reviewer decision with minimized content retention. Escalate imminent threats, sexual exploitation or grooming indicators, self-harm/violence threats, doxxing, illegal content, and repeat evasion to the duty officer; preserve only necessary evidence under a documented legal hold. Provide an appeal/correction path, but do not disclose detection thresholds. UK Online Safety Act applicability, duties, age assurance, reporting, and record-keeping require counsel and current Ofcom/official verification [4] [5]. The ICO Children’s Code is statutory guidance for services likely to be accessed by children and calls for best interests, DPIA, high-privacy defaults, minimization, parental controls, profiling safeguards, and no harmful nudges [1].

7. **Incident command and communications — [Incident commander + communications owner]**: Maintain severity definitions, an on-call rota, contact tree, decision log, evidence-preservation procedure, and pre-approved internal, player, regulator, and partner templates. In the first phase, confirm scope, protect players, contain without destroying evidence, and establish a single source of truth; then issue factual updates at a fixed cadence even when investigation is incomplete. Communicate what happened, affected periods/features, current protections, player actions, support route, and next update time; avoid speculation, blame, or promises not supported by evidence. For a data incident, run the UK GDPR breach-assessment and notification workflow with counsel/DPO; the ICO states that notifiable breaches generally must be reported without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of awareness [6]. NCSC recommends planning communications before, during, and after a cyber incident [3].

8. **Observability and audit — [Platform owner]**: Emit correlation IDs across request, model generation, policy decision, ledger append, projection, migration, support action, and notification. Monitor migration lag/error rate, save-load failures, ledger/projection divergence, backup freshness, restore-test results, moderation false negatives/positives, escalation latency, appeal outcomes, and incident-update timeliness. Keep dashboards segmented by adult/Kid Mode and release cohort, with privacy-preserving aggregation and access reviews.

9. **Governance and launch control — [Product accountable executive + DPO + security + safeguarding]**: Maintain a risk register and signed go/no-go checklist covering DPIA, age-appropriate design, policy content, model evaluations, abuse red-team results, recovery tests, support readiness, accessibility, and incident communications. Label legal, store, age-assurance, advertising, and reporting conclusions as **pending counsel/official verification**, especially because “adult Free” does not remove the possibility that children access the service and “Kid Mode” may create child-data and safety obligations.
output.risks: Primary failure modes are destructive or non-idempotent migrations that corrupt or silently erase saves; code rollback without data rollback; backups that exist but cannot restore a coherent ledger and projection; compromised backup credentials; support tooling that exposes child or sensitive content; AI policy bypasses, grooming, self-harm, sexual, violent, or privacy harms; weak age-mode separation; over-retention of transcripts; inconsistent enforcement across model versions; slow or misleading incident communications; and regulatory, contractual, or store-policy noncompliance. A web service may be “likely to be accessed by children” even when marketed to adults, so scope and duties must be confirmed with UK counsel, the DPO, Ofcom, and current official guidance.
